summary: Colonial powers and then the United States negotiated with Native nations as diplomatic powers while asserting an exclusive federal right to acquire Indian land (Doctrine of Discovery). Office of Indian Affairs created in the War Department on March 11, 1824. Ratified treaties run 1778-1871 (BIA counts 370 ratified, at least 45 unratified).
key_acts: Trade and Intercourse Act 1790 (1 Stat. 137, from-memory); Johnson v. M'Intosh, 21 U.S. (8 Wheat.) 543 (1823); Calhoun order creating Office of Indian Affairs (Mar 11, 1824)
land_effect: Early cessions east of the Mississippi; federal monopoly on purchasing Indian land; no reliable single acreage total (see D3 range of about 1 to 1.5+ billion acres ceded over all eras, disputed)

summary: Federal policy to move eastern nations west of the Mississippi through removal treaties and military force. Office of Indian Affairs gained a statutory Commissioner (Jul 9, 1832). Gover's 2000 apology named removal marches.
key_acts: Indian Removal Act, May 28, 1830 (4 Stat. 411); Treaty of Dancing Rabbit Creek (Sept 27, 1830); Treaty of New Echota (1835); Worcester v. Georgia, 31 U.S. (6 Pet.) 515 (1832); Commissioner of Indian Affairs statute, Jul 9, 1832 (4 Stat. 564)
land_effect: More than 60,000 people from at least 18 tribes forced west under Jackson and Van Buren (secondary source); about 3,000 Seminoles removed in Second Seminole War; large eastern cessions (no verified acreage total)

summary: Federal policy to confine nations to defined reservations to open land for settlement, railroads and mining. Congress ended treaty-making on March 3, 1871 (25 U.S.C. 71) while preserving existing treaty obligations; agreements and executive orders followed. Board of Indian Commissioners created 1869. Office of Indian Affairs moved to Interior in 1849.
key_acts: Indian Appropriations Act 1851 (9 Stat. 574, from-memory); transfer to Interior Mar 3, 1849 (9 Stat. 395); Board of Indian Commissioners Apr 10, 1869 (16 Stat. 40); treaty-ending rider Mar 3, 1871 (16 Stat. 566; 25 U.S.C. 71); Black Hills taken Feb 28, 1877; Lone Wolf v. Hitchcock, 187 U.S. 553 (1903) later confirmed plenary power
land_effect: Reservations carved from larger territories then shrunk by agreement, executive order and statute; Wilson 1935 reports original reservation acreage of 130,730,190 plus 9,106,312 added (maximum tribal acreage 139,836,502 up to Sept 1934); Black Hills taking held unconstitutional in U.S. v. Sioux Nation, 448 U.S. 371 (1980)

summary: Federal policy to break up communal reservation land into individual allotments, declare the remainder surplus for non-Indian settlement, and assimilate Native people through boarding schools and citizenship. Boarding schools: 408 identified in Volume I (2022), 417 institutions in Volume II (2024), 1819-1969.
key_acts: General Allotment (Dawes) Act, Feb 8, 1887 (24 Stat. 388); Curtis Act 1898; Dead Indian Act 1902; Burke Act 1906; Lone Wolf v. Hitchcock (1903); Indian Citizenship Act 1924; Meriam Report 1928
land_effect: Widely cited: about 138 million acres (1887) to about 48 million acres (1934), a loss of about 90 million acres (secondary sources; primary not found). Wilson 1935 Table VII: 40,848,172 acres allotted; 23,225,472 alienated from trust; 22,694,658 surplus opened to settlement. Fractionation of heirship land begins.

summary: John Collier's reorientation: end allotment, allow tribes to organize governments under federal-model constitutions and to receive land into trust. Board of Indian Commissioners ended 1933. Tribal votes on the Act were mixed (172 accepted/75 rejected per one count; 174/78 per another).
key_acts: Indian Reorganization Act, Jun 18, 1934 (48 Stat. 984; 25 U.S.C. 5101 et seq.; Section 5 at 25 U.S.C. 5108); Carcieri v. Salazar, 555 U.S. 379 (2009) limits Section 5 to tribes under federal jurisdiction in 1934
land_effect: Allotment halted; secondary source reports more than 2 million acres returned to tribes in first 20 years (unchecked against primary); beginning of modern fee-to-trust

summary: Federal policy to end federal supervision and the trust relationship with tribes, transfer jurisdiction to states, and relocate Native people to cities. Run-up from 1945; Indian Claims Commission created Aug 13, 1946; officially repudiated by President Nixon on July 8, 1970.
key_acts: House Concurrent Resolution 108 (Aug 1, 1953); Public Law 280 (Aug 15, 1953; 67 Stat. 588); Menominee Termination Act 1954; Klamath Termination Act (Aug 13, 1954); Western Oregon Indian Termination Act 1954; Indian Relocation Act 1956; California Rancheria Termination Act 1958; Indian Claims Commission Act (1946)
land_effect: Figures disagree: NARA says 60 termination proceedings 1953-1970 and over 3 million acres relinquished; Wikipedia says more than 100 tribes and bands and about 2.5 million acres out of trust; about 12,000 people affected. Pick-Sloan dams flooded about 356,254 acres on seven reservations (1944-1966).

summary: Federal policy shift toward tribal control of programs and away from termination, announced in Nixon's July 8, 1970 message. Targeted land restorations alongside continued fractionation.
key_acts: Blue Lake return (signed Dec 15, 1970; 48,000 acres to Taos Pueblo); Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act (Dec 18, 1971; 85 Stat. 688); Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (Pub. L. 93-638, Jan 4, 1975; 88 Stat. 2203); Indian Child Welfare Act 1978 and AIRFA 1978 (from-memory); Hodel v. Irving, 481 U.S. 704 (1987)
land_effect: Blue Lake 48,000 acres returned; ANCSA about 45 million acres and about $962.5 million to Alaska Native corporations (commonly cited as 44 million acres); restored terminated tribes (Menominee 1973, Klamath 1986); ILCA escheat struck down (fractionation continues)

summary: Federal policy letting tribes receive funds in bulk and redesign programs with less federal oversight; trust reform and repatriation law begin. Indian Gaming Regulatory Act (1988, from-memory) sets Oct 17, 1988 cutoff for after-acquired gaming land.
key_acts: ISDEAA amendments 1988 (from-memory); Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act (Nov 16, 1990; 25 U.S.C. 3001 et seq.); Tribal Self-Governance Act of 1994 (Title II of Pub. L. 103-413, Oct 25, 1994; 108 Stat. 4270); American Indian Trust Fund Management Reform Act 1994 (created Office of the Special Trustee); Cobell v. Babbitt filed Jun 10, 1996
land_effect: Primarily governance and legal accountability, not large land changes; gaming revenue later funds tribal land purchases; trust fund litigation begins

era_name: Contemporary: Repair, Repatriation, Co-Stewardship, and Land Back
summary: Acknowledgment of harms, trust accountability, return of remains and some land, co-stewardship of federal lands, and renewed litigation and legislation. Apology by BIA head Kevin Gover (Sept 8, 2000); Cobell settlement final Nov 24, 2012; Land Buy-Back 2013-2022; McGirt (2020); Interior boarding school reports (2022, 2024); Biden apology (Oct 25, 2024); Lumbee recognized by FY2026 NDAA (Dec 18, 2025); 575 entries on Jan 30, 2026 list; Alaska trust authority revoked by Solicitor's opinion M-37087 (Feb 24, 2026).
key_acts: Cobell settlement via Claims Resolution Act of 2010 ($3.4 billion); Carcieri v. Salazar (2009); McGirt v. Oklahoma, 591 U.S. ___ (Jul 9, 2020); National Bison Range restoration (Pub. L. 116-260); Joint Secretarial Order 3403 (2021); revised 25 CFR Part 151 (effective Jan 11, 2024); Truth and Healing Commission on Indian Boarding School Policies Act, S. 761 (119th Cong., reported Jul 31, 2025; no enactment found)
land_effect: Trust base about 56 million surface acres (BIA, current); Land Buy-Back consolidated about 2.3 to 3 million acre-equivalents of fractional interests (figures differ by date); Bison Range 18,800.22 acres; Interior reported 400 co-stewardship agreements by Dec 9, 2024; other returns listed in secondary sources and not individually verified
